1  For Respondents : M/s.S.T.Varadarajulu for R1  ORDER
This Writ Petition is filed for issuance of Writ of Certiorari to call for the records pertaining to the award dated 07.06.2013 made in I.D.No.255 of 2007.
2. The facts in brief are that the petitioner has joined as a Driver with Staff No.D15296 on 02.09.1990 in the second respondent corporation.

On 20.07.2003, when the petitioner was driving a bus in route No.C.70, from Redhills to Guindy, at about 11.00 a.m., MMDA Colony, near Vinaygapuram Junction, a lorry came in the opposite direction and suddenly took U-turn and turned in the direction in which the petitioner was driving.
The petitioner applied brake and turned the vehicle towards left side to avoid colliding with the lorry.

The brake pedal came out and the bus did not stop and dashed against the left side body of the lorry and dashed against the hotel on the left side of the road, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and EB-Box and five pedestrians who thereby sustained injuries and died.
3. A charge memo was issued to the petitioner on 25.07.2003, alleging that the accident had occurred on account of his negligence.
The petitioner has submitted his explanation on 09.09.2003 and domestic enquiry was conducted and finally the petitioner was terminated from service on 02.05.2006.

4. The petitioner has raised Industrial Dispute in I.D.No.225 of 2007 and filed an application before the Labour Court/ first respondent seeking to set aside the dismissal order and to reinstate him back into service with full wages.
The said petition was allowed and award was passed on 07.06.2013 directing the second respondent to pay compensation of Rs.3,00,000/-.
However, the Tribunal has declined to order reinstatement with continuity of service and backwages and therefore sought for suitable directions.

5. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner/corporation that the order passed by the Labour Court dated https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 07.06.2013 in I.D.No.225 of 2007 setting aside the termination orders and is erroneous compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- awarded is on the higher side.
6.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioner that the rash and negligent driving of the petitioner is responsible for the accident in which five persons have lost their lives and that he has got a bad track record in respect of accident.
It is the submitted that when suspension was revoked for some period, during that period, also he has caused another accident in which one person died.
The Labour Court has not properly analysed the report of enquiry officer and has set aside the order of termination of the petitioner.

2
7. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned counsel for the First respondent and perused the materials placed on record.

8. The two grounds on which the Labour Court has set aside the termination orders are that the Criminal Court has found that the first respondent/driver was not guilty of rash and negligent driving and that https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the petitioner/corporation itself filed a counter before the Motor Vehicle Accidents Tribunal stated that the accident has occurred on account of mechanical failure and not on account of rash and negligent act of the first respondent/Driver.

As per counter affidavit filed by the Management, in the Motor Vehicle Accident Tribunal when the petitioner was driving the vehicle, the other vehicle which was coming in opposite direction has suddenly took U-turn and turned the vehicle toward the side in which the petitioner's vehicle was proceeding, on account of which, the first respondent had to applied sudden brakes, thereby the brake pedal came out of the lever rod, thereby causing accident in which five persons died by sustaining grievous injuries.
Hence, the contention of the petitioner/corporation that the Labour Court has come to a wrong conclusion by setting aside the termination of the Driver from service is not acceptable.

9. In view of the above discussions, this Court finds no reason to Dr.D.NAGARJUN, J.
j a i i n t e r f e r e w i t h t h e f i n d i n g t h e L a b o u r C o u r t a n d t h e s a m e i s c o n f i r m e d .
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
Accordingly, the Writ Petition is dismissed.
No costs.
